marks.gloss_en: רבי מאיר היא, דאמר: מצוה לקיים דברי המת
if he said 'if they die, others inherit in their place' -- whether he said 'give' or 'give only' -- they are given only a shekel
Rava: because the soldiers of Mechoza are many
Ilfa and R' Yochanan, hard-pressed: let us go and trade, and fulfil in ourselves 'however there shall be no needy among you' (Deut 15:4)
the first angel: let us throw this wall on them and kill them, for they leave eternal life and occupy themselves with temporal life
R' Yochanan: I will go back and fulfil in myself 'for the needy shall not cease from the land' (Deut 15:11)
they said to Ilfa: had the Master sat and studied, would the Master not have become head?
one who says 'give a shekel to my sons each week', and they are fit to be given a sela -- they are given a sela
they said of Nachum Ish Gam Zu that he was blind in both eyes, without both hands and both legs, his whole body full of boils, and lay in a shaky house
his students: Rabbi, since you are wholly righteous, why has this befallen you?

Nachum: I fell on his face and said: may my eyes that had no pity on your eyes be blinded, my hands be cut off, my legs be cut off; my mind did not rest until I said: may my whole body be full of boils
why was he called Nachum Ish Gam Zu? because of everything that befell him he would say: this too is for good
the king, wishing to kill them all: the Jews are mocking me
a province they could not conquer: they tried the dust and conquered it; they filled his chest with jewels and sent him with great honour
Nachum to the innkeepers: what I took from here I brought there
[the 1500-city:] if [the nine died] in one day or in four days -- this is not a pestilence
the mishna (cited): what is a pestilence? a city that sends out five hundred foot-soldiers, etc.
